title: Unicode escapes spell whole characters
description: No string or member name holds a \u escape in the range \uD800 to \uDFFF without its pair. Such an escape spells half a Unicode character, so the text is not valid Unicode and cannot be written as UTF-8. Escapes are how such a character reaches a candidate that utf8-encoded accepts, since no valid UTF-8 byte sequence can carry one. Only escapes are judged here: bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are utf8-encoded's, and the noncharacters are valid text and are not refused. RFC 8259 admits an unpaired surrogate in its own grammar, so a conformant parser accepts one and implementations then differ over what they do with a string they cannot encode; I-JSON (RFC 7493) is the profile that forbids it.
summary: Every `\u` escape spells a whole Unicode character
